thread.title: Technology Sector Update for 11/15/2018: NTES, CSCO, MARK

author: MT Newswires
title: Technology Sector Update for 11/15/2018: NTES, CSCO, MARK
text:

Technology stocks were rebounding today following two days of steep loses, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding over 1.8% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising more than 3%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) NetEase ( NTES ) rose over 5% in Thursday's afternoon trade after the Chinese online gaming company reported non-GAAP Q3 net income exceeding Wall Street expectations and authorized a new, $1 billion stock buyback program over the next year beginning Friday, Nov. 16. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $2.55 per American depositary share during the September quarter, down from $3.32 per share during the same quarter last year but still beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. Revenue increased to RMB16.86 billion, or about $2.45 billion, compared with RMB12.48 billion during the year-ago period and roughly matching the $2.42 billion Street view.
In other sector news:
(+) Cisco ( CSCO ) was more than 5% higher Thursday afternoon after the networking equipment company reported non-GAAP Q1 net income of $0.75 per share, improving on a $0.61 per share adjusted profit during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.03 per share. Revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $13.1 billion, also topping the $12.86 billion analyst mean. Cisco also is expecting Q2 financial results straddling the Street view looking for non-GAAP net income of $0.72 per share on 5.4% revenue growth to $12.53 million.
(-) Remark Holdings ( MARK ) dropped to a new all-time low on Thursday, sinking over 40% to a worst-ever $1.95 a share after the artificial intelligence company late Wednesday reported Q3 revenue trailing analyst expectations. Revenue during the three months ended Sept. 30 was unchanged from the same quarter last year at $19.4 million, falling $4.3 million shy of the single analyst call. The company also is projecting Q4 in a range of $19 million to $23 million compared with the single-analyst call expecting $27.13 million.
